claims.quote: Diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates with normal heart size ARDS (PCWP <18, P/F <300)

claims.quote: C - Cardiac: CT ratio <50% on PA (<60% on AP); contour; valves; pacemaker leads.

claims.text: Berlin criteria: onset within 1 week of a known insult or new or worsening respiratory symptoms; imaging: bilateral opacities not fully explained by effusions, lobar or lung collapse, or nodules
claims.quote: Timing | Onset within 1 week of known insult or of new or worsening respiratory symptoms | Imaging (radiograph or CT of chest) | Bilateral opacities not fully explained by effusions, lobar or lung collapse, or nodules

claims.text: Berlin severity: mild 200 < PaO2/FIO2 ≤ 300 mm Hg with PEEP or CPAP ≥ 5 cm H2O; moderate 100 < PaO2/FIO2 ≤ 200 with PEEP ≥ 5; severe PaO2/FIO2 ≤ 100 with PEEP ≥ 5
claims.quote: Mild | 200 mm Hg < PaO2/FIO2≤ 300 mm Hg* with PEEP or CPAP ≥ 5 cm H2O | Moderate | 100 mm Hg < PaO2/FIO2≤ 200 mm Hg with PEEP ≥ 5 cm H2O | Severe | PaO2/FIO2≤ 100 mm Hg with PEEP ≥ 5 cm H2O

claims.text: Versus cardiogenic edema: LV failure is suggested by an S3, JVD and peripheral edema plus diffuse central infiltrates, cardiomegaly and an abnormally wide vascular pedicle on CXR; the diffuse bilateral opacities of ARDS are generally more peripheral
claims.quote: High-pressure pulmonary edema due to left ventricular failure is suggested by a third heart sound (S3), jugular venous distention, and peripheral edema on examination and by the presence of diffuse central infiltrates, cardiomegaly, and an abnormally wide vascular pedicle on chest radiograph. The diffuse, bilateral opacities of ARDS are generally more peripheral.

claims.text: Causes A type of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure caused by diffuse, inflammatory lung injury
claims.quote: Acute respiratory distress syndrome is a type of AHRF that is caused by diffuse, inflammatory lung injury.

claims.text: Causes may involve direct or indirect lung injury
claims.quote: Causes of ARDS may involve direct or indirect lung injury.

claims.text: Sepsis and pneumonia account for the majority of ARDS
claims.quote: Sepsis and pneumonia account for the majority of ARDS (4, 5).

claims.text: Acute hypoxemia may cause dyspnea, restlessness and anxiety; signs include confusion or altered consciousness, cyanosis, tachypnea, tachycardia and diaphoresis
claims.quote: Acute hypoxemia (see also Oxygen Desaturation) may cause dyspnea, restlessness, and anxiety. Signs include confusion or alteration of consciousness, cyanosis, tachypnea, tachycardia, and diaphoresis.

claims.text: Crackles, typically diffuse but sometimes worse at the lung bases (particularly the left lower lobe)
claims.quote: Inspiratory opening of closed airways causes crackles, detected during chest auscultation; the crackles are typically diffuse but sometimes worse at the lung bases, particularly in the left lower lobe because the weight of the heart increases atelectasis.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: lung-protective ventilation (6 mL/kg IBW)
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Cardiac / Vascular / PE table

claims.text: Lower tidal volumes reduce mortality: in most patients set tidal volume at or below 6 mL/kg ideal body weight, which requires a higher respiratory rate, even up to 35/minute
claims.quote: It is clear that ventilating with lower tidal volumes reduces mortality. Accordingly, in most patients, tidal volume should be set at or below 6 mL/kg ideal body weight (see sidebar Initial Ventilator Management in ARDS). This setting necessitates an increase in respiratory rate, even up to 35/minute, to produce sufficient alveolar ventilation to allow for adequate carbon dioxide removal.

claims.text: Check plateau pressure every 4 hours and after each PEEP or tidal volume change; target < 30 cm H2O with normal chest wall compliance
claims.quote: The best indicator of alveolar overdistention is measurement of a plateau pressure through an end-inspiratory hold maneuver; plateau pressure should be checked every 4 hours and after each change in PEEP or tidal volume. The target plateau pressure is < 30 cm H2O in patients with normal chest wall compliance.
